info.title: mashctl
info.description: Speaks for the mesh, through a server: set it up, check it, make and remove endpoints.

command.name: mashctl
command.description: Administers a mash mesh through a server.

options.description: The server address. May be given more than once.

metadata.name: x-today
metadata.value: Replaces mashctl adopt, mashctl init and mashctl init --local. mashctl does not install or start NATS; the NATS quick-start script writes this file as its last step.

metadata.name: x-notes
metadata.value: Safe to run again. THE SETUP FILE is YAML, and holds paths, never secrets: 'servers' (a list of addresses), 'ca' (the certificate authority's certificate, if the server uses its own), 'owner' (the first owner), 'admin_creds' (the administrator's creds file), 'system_creds' (the system account's creds file), 'operator_key' (the operator's signing key) and 'account_key' (the account's signing key). The last three are what cancelling a deleted endpoint's key needs. A hosted NATS where you do not hold the operator key, such as Synadia Cloud, is not supported by mashctl in 0.5.6; mash itself works against any conforming server.

commands.name: create
commands.description: Create an endpoint and its credentials.

options.name: --out
options.description: Write a join file for another machine and install nothing here.

options.description: Sign this public key and make no seed. Needs --out. For an endpoint that made its own key with mash key create.
